raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-ALB-CitizenServiceDelivery",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Procurement capacity is weak because ADISA is a newly created agency, increasing the chance of procurement errors and delays.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a fully staffed PMU with a dedicated Procurement Specialist, use Bank‑provided sample TORs, and involve Bank technical experts in review.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risk rating is High. Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Financial management risk is substantial due to ADISA and MIPA lacking experience with large donor‑funded operations.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit qualified finance specialists, provide on‑the‑job training on Bank fiduciary rules, and develop a detailed Financial Management Manual.",
      "evidence": "The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial... ADISA... have no previous experience... capacity strengthening recommended."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "The project’s compressed implementation timeline may cause delays in CSC construction and reform milestones.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement phased work plans with clear milestones, monitor progress weekly, and maintain contingency buffers in the schedule.",
      "evidence": "The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk, which is mitigated by the project’s span and incentives to deliver up to 2020."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Integration of legacy registers and new IT systems is technically complex; many agencies currently have no IT systems.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Adopt a phased IT development approach, provide technical assistance, conduct rigorous testing, and ensure interoperability standards via NAIS.",
      "evidence": "Seven institutions... have no IT system in place... building new IT systems... will be carried out in phases."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Bureaucratic resistance to ceding front‑office functions may impede reform implementation.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Launch a change‑management program, engage staff through incentives, and communicate benefits via the communication strategy.",
      "evidence": "Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts to improve back‑office functions... diagnostics of the political economy of reforms and a focus on change management can help."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Weak coordination among numerous ministries, agencies, and committees could lead to duplicated effort or stalled decisions.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Strengthen the steering and inter‑ministerial committees, define clear roles, and hold regular joint meetings with documented action items.",
      "evidence": "Inter‑agency coordination... Inter‑Ministerial Public Services Committee... Technical Inter‑ministerial Committee... PMU will coordinate."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Low internet penetration limits citizen uptake of e‑services, risking under‑utilization of digital reforms.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Maintain physical CSCs, expand assisted access points (internet cafés, community centers), and run outreach campaigns for non‑digital channels.",
      "evidence": "Only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013... need for physical presence... assisted digital access."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Construction of the new Citizen Service Center may cause dust, noise, waste, and traffic impacts.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement the approved Environmental Management Plan, enforce construction best practices, and monitor compliance through regular site inspections.",
      "evidence": "Potential environmental impacts... dust and noise, waste generation... mitigated through sound construction practices and implementation of a project specific EMP."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Emphasis on high‑end urban CSCs and online services could marginalize poor, vulnerable, and rural populations.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide assisted digital access, retain existing service points, and run targeted information campaigns for disadvantaged groups.",
      "evidence": "Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art means... could diminish access of the poor and vulnerable... project takes proactive steps to enhance access."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Results‑Based Financing disbursements are blocked until DLI#5 is achieved, risking cash‑flow shortfalls.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Prioritize completion of the Reform Policy Document and baseline survey, provide technical assistance, and monitor DLI#5 progress closely.",
      "evidence": "No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "High perceived corruption may undermine citizen trust and the effectiveness of service‑delivery reforms.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Deploy the citizen feedback mechanism, publicize anti‑corruption results, and strengthen transparency through performance dashboards.",
      "evidence": "Corruption... second biggest problem... project aims to reduce petty corruption and improve service quality."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Key PMU positions remain vacant at project start, limiting operational capacity.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Accelerate recruitment of Procurement and Administrative Specialists, use interim staff, and obtain Bank support for capacity building.",
      "evidence": "Except for the Financial Specialist, PMU staff are yet to be contracted due to the delay in the approval of the PPF."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Reliance on external consultants for ICT and process re‑engineering may cause delays or quality issues.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop clear TORs, apply QCBS/QBS selection, and monitor deliverables against milestones with third‑party validation.",
      "evidence": "Consulting services will be determined... selection methods include QCBS, QBS, etc."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "RBF eligible expenditures are limited to salaries and social security; payroll delays could affect disbursements.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Synchronize payroll processing with FMIS, ensure timely submission of payroll data, and conduct regular payroll audits.",
      "evidence": "EEPs for this project are salaries and social security contributions... processed through the government’s FMIS."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Potential changes in political leadership could reduce commitment to the reform agenda.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Embed reforms in legislation, secure approvals from the Strategic Planning Committee and Prime Minister, and maintain broad stakeholder buy‑in.",
      "evidence": "High level political commitment... Prime Minister and Council of Ministers have declared this initiative a key priority."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Data quality problems in legacy registers (e.g., missing National ID numbers) may hinder automation and service delivery.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct comprehensive data cleaning, digitization, and validation; align registers with NAIS standards and implement data‑quality checks.",
      "evidence": "National ID number is missing for most records... only 45‑50% of the archive digitized; legal issues over ownership remain."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R17",
      "description": "Involvement of private partners in CSC construction/operation could lead to contract disputes and cost overruns.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Use transparent procurement procedures, define clear PPP terms, and involve legal counsel to oversee contract negotiations.",
      "evidence": "Various models for financing, construction and management, including public‑private partnerships (PPPs), are under consideration."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Procurement capacity is weak because ADISA is a newly created agency, increasing the chance of procurement errors and delays.

risks.evidence: Procurement risk rating is High. Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency.
